t.1.190.1: Without having heard these words of yours, great seer, I had earlier striven to bring about this matter. One cannot turn away from what has been ordained; so this very ordinance has come to pass as fitting.
t.1.190.2: The knot of fate cannot be undone; nothing here is ordained by one's own deeds. The token was set up for the sake of a single bridegroom, yet that very thing has now come to befit many.
t.1.190.4: If this has been ordained by Śaṃkara, whether it be dharma or adharma, the fault here is not mine. Let these men take her hand according to the rite, as they please, for Kṛṣṇā has been destined for them.
t.1.190.3: Just as Kṛṣṇā had spoken before, saying, "May the Blessed One give me many husbands," so too did he pronounce the boon to her, for the god knows what is highest in this matter.
t.1.190.5: Then the blessed one said to the Dharmarāja: "Today is an auspicious day, O son of Pāṇḍu; today the moon enters into conjunction with Pauṣya. Take Kṛṣṇā's hand today, you first."
t.1.190.7: Then all his friends, his counsellors and ministers came together there, supremely delighted, to see the wedding, and so did the brahmins and the townspeople, each according to his rank.
t.1.190.6: Then King Yajñasena, together with his sons, gathered a great store of every choicest thing suited to the wedding, and brought forth his daughter Kṛṣṇā, having bathed her and adorned her with many jewels.
t.1.190.8: That dwelling of his, graced by crowds of supplicants, its courtyard adorned with scattered lotuses and water lilies, and variegated with heaps of costly jewels, shone like the sky studded with spotless stars.
t.1.190.9: Then those sons of the Kaurava king, young men adorned with ornaments and wearing earrings, clad in costly garments and sprinkled with the finest sandalwood, having bathed and performed the auspicious rites, came forth.
t.1.190.10: Together with Dhaumya, their family priest, whose splendor equalled that of fire, they all, O lord, entered that hall one after another in due order, rejoicing like great bulls entering a cow-pen.
t.1.190.11: Then he who had mastered the Vedas, having kindled and laid the fire, offered oblations with mantras into the blazing fire; and the knower of mantras, leading Yudhiṣṭhira forward, joined him together with Kṛṣṇā.
t.1.190.12: That master of the Vedas led the two, their hands clasped together, around the fire in the auspicious sunwise direction. Then, having taken leave of him who shone in battle, the family priest departed from the king's palace.
t.1.190.14: And there the brahmin seer spoke of this supreme, wondrous thing that surpasses the human: that glorious, slender-waisted lady, it is said, became a virgin again as each day passed.
t.1.190.13: And in this order, day after day, those sons of a king, great chariot-warriors of the finest form who increased the Kaurava line, then took the hand of that excellent woman.
t.1.190.15: When the marriage had been performed, Drupada gave to the great chariot-warriors excellent wealth of many forms: a hundred chariots adorned with fine gold, each yoked to four horses and garlanded with golden bridles.
t.1.190.17: And to each of them separately, with the fire as witness, Saumaki gave wealth amounting to a hundred thousand, and likewise garments and ornaments of great splendour and very great value.
t.1.190.18: And when the marriage had been performed, the Pāṇḍavas, mighty and like Indra, having obtained that fortune abounding in jewels, took their pleasure in the city of that king of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.190.16: He gave a hundred elephants marked with lotus spots, a hundred like mountains with golden peaks, and likewise a hundred slave-girls in the first bloom of youth, adorned with costly attire, ornaments, garments and garlands.
